---
title: "What we found across all questions"
subtitle: "Eight findings, each with what we measured, what it means and what to be careful about"
---

```{r}
source("_common.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
med_B <- median(idx$ratio_B, na.rm = TRUE); med_C <- median(idx$ratio_C, na.rm = TRUE)
same_B <- sum(idx$A_direct == idx$B_annif & idx$question_id %in% usable_q)
jac <- function(c) ov_A$jaccard[ov_A$condition_b == c & ov_A$question_id %in% usable_q]
push_C <- ov_A[ov_A$condition_b == "C_finto" & ov_A$question_id %in% usable_q, ]
```

::: {.in-short}
**In short.** Across the `r length(usable_q)` questions that found records (out of `r n_q`):

1. the fullest search matches far more records;
2. it shows mostly different records;
3. Annif often frames the question in its own way;
4. other institutions come forward;
5. so do Finnish- and Swedish-language records;
6. the types of material shift towards texts and artworks;
7. the subject words change a lot;
8. in some questions the period covered moves.

Whether the new records are *better* is not yet known: that needs the
[human checking](human-check.qmd).
:::

`r left_out_text()`

## 1. The fullest search matches many more records

**What we measured.** For each search, how many records in the whole Finna index match it.
This shows how wide the "net" is.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| fig-alt: "Dot chart: matching records in Finna for searches A, B and C, per question, on a log scale."
dot_chart(idx, "Matching records in the Finna index (log scale)", log = TRUE, order_ids = qids)
```
<p class="how-to-read">How to read this: each row is a question, each dot a search. Further right
means more matching records. The scale jumps by ten at each step (1, 10, 100, 1000). An open
circle at the far left means the search matched nothing.</p>

**What it means.** Compared with our own words (A):

- with Annif's words (B), the middle question matched **`r times(med_B)`** as many records;
- with the thesaurus terms (C), it matched **`r times(med_C)`** as many.

In `r same_B` of the `r length(usable_q)` questions, Annif's words did not change the number
of matches at all.

**Be careful.** More matching records does not mean better ones. A wider net also catches
more that is off topic. `r if (newer_than("0.3.0")) "In the first run, Annif's *Finland* turned the [Swedish-language theatre](questions.qmd#finland-swedish-theatre) search into any theatre in Finland; this run no longer adds such partial words (see [Problems to fix](problems.qmd))." else "The [Swedish-language theatre](questions.qmd#finland-swedish-theatre) question shows how a wider search can drift away from the question."`

## 2. Wider searches show different records

**What we measured.** How many of the 60 kept records two searches have in common (the
**overlap**: records found by both, divided by records found by either).

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-alt: "Dot chart: overlap of search B and search C with search A, per question."
o <- data.frame(question_id = usable_q,
                A_direct = NA,
                B_annif = ov_A$jaccard[ov_A$condition_b == "B_annif"][match(usable_q, ov_A$question_id[ov_A$condition_b == "B_annif"])],
                C_finto = ov_A$jaccard[ov_A$condition_b == "C_finto"][match(usable_q, ov_A$question_id[ov_A$condition_b == "C_finto"])])
dot_chart(o, "Share of records in common with search A (0 = none, 1 = all)", xlim = c(0, 1), show = c("B_annif", "C_finto"))
```
<p class="how-to-read">How to read this: a dot at 1 means the search showed exactly the same
records as search A; a dot near 0 means almost entirely different records.</p>

**What it means.** On average, search B shares **`r pct(mean(jac("B_annif"), na.rm = TRUE))`**
of its records with A, and search C only **`r pct(mean(jac("C_finto"), na.rm = TRUE))`**.
Because each search keeps only 60 records, the wider search C also **pushed out** records:
on average `r num(mean(push_C$only_a))` of the records that A showed are missing from C.

**Be careful.** The overlap only tells us the records are different. Whether those
"pushed out" records mattered for the question is for the human checkers to judge.

## 3. Annif often frames the question in its own way

**What we measured.** Every subject word Annif suggested, and whether it fitted one of the
researcher's key words.

```{r}
m <- as.data.frame(table(factor(annif$fits, fits_levels)))
m <- m[m$Freq > 0 | m$Var1 != "only part of your word (not used)", ]
m$share <- pct(m$Freq / sum(m$Freq))
tbl(m, c("What happened to Annif's suggestion", "Number", "Share"))
hist_n <- length(unique(annif$question_id[annif$label == "history"]))
un <- annif[annif$mapping == "unanchored" & annif$label != "history", ]
un <- un[order(-un$score), ]
ex_un <- head(un[!duplicated(un$label), ], 8)
```

**What it means.** Most suggestions (`r pct(mean(annif$mapping == "unanchored"))`) did not fit
the researcher's words. Annif suggested **history** for `r hist_n` of the `r n_q` questions: it
reads "how did X change" as a question about history in general. Other suggestions that did
not fit show a different way of describing the topic:
`r paste0("*", ex_un$label, "* (", qname(ex_un$question_id), ")", collapse = "; ")`.

These words were **not searched** in this study. They are a finding in themselves: they show
how an automatic indexer would redraw the question's boundaries. For the
[Karelian evacuees](questions.qmd#karelian-evacuees) question, Annif's *internally displaced
persons* is in fact the official term, while the everyday word *evacuees* found nothing.
`r if ("finland-swedish-theatre" %in% empty_q && any(annif$question_id == "finland-swedish-theatre" & annif$label == "Swedish-speaking Finns")) "Likewise, for [Swedish-language theatre](questions.qmd#finland-swedish-theatre) Annif suggested *Swedish-speaking Finns*, the thesaurus's name for the group, while the everyday *Finland Swedes* found nothing." else ""`

## 4. Other institutions come forward

**What we measured.** Which museum, archive or library each record comes from. We compare the
mix of institutions between searches with a 0-to-1 **difference score** (0 = same mix,
1 = completely different; see the [word list](how-it-works.qmd#words-used-in-this-report)).

```{r}
inst <- vis[vis$dimension == "institution" & vis$from == "A_direct" & vis$question_id %in% usable_q, ]
w <- data.frame(Question = qname(usable_q))
for (c in c("B_annif", "C_finto")) {
  r <- inst[inst$to == c, ][match(usable_q, inst$question_id[inst$to == c]), ]
  w[[paste(cond_short[c], "difference")]] <- num(r$jsd, 2)
}
ic <- reshape(metrics[, c("question_id", "condition", "institutions")], idvar = "question_id", timevar = "condition", direction = "wide")
ic <- ic[match(usable_q, ic$question_id), ]
w$`Institutions in A` <- ic$institutions.A_direct
w$`Institutions in C` <- ic$institutions.C_finto
rC <- inst[inst$to == "C_finto", ][match(usable_q, inst$question_id[inst$to == "C_finto"]), ]
w$`New in C (examples)` <- ifelse(is.na(rC$examples_gained), "", rC$examples_gained)
tbl(w)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart: the 12 institutions with most records, share of records in searches A, B and C, all questions together."
draw_group_bars(pooled_counts("institution"), pooled_n(), top = 12)
```
<p class="how-to-read">How to read this: all questions together, the twelve institutions with the
most records. Each group of bars is one institution; the bars show its share of each search's
records, and the number is the record count. Purple, bold names appear only in B or C; grey names
disappear in C. Charts for each question are on [Compare searches](compare.qmd).</p>

**What it means.** The median difference score for institutions between A and C is
**`r num(median(inst$jsd[inst$to == "C_finto"], na.rm = TRUE), 2)`**, against
`r num(median(inst$jsd[inst$to == "B_annif"], na.rm = TRUE), 2)` between A and B. The
thesaurus terms reach collections that our own English words do not, often regional museums
and specialist archives whose records are written in Finnish or Swedish.
`r noise_sentence(inst, "institutions")`

**Be careful.** These are the institutions among 60 records per search, not across all of
Finna. A museum that is "new in C" may well have more relevant material that no search
showed.

## 5. Finnish- and Swedish-language records come forward

**What we measured.** The language of each record, where Finna gives one.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| fig-alt: "Stacked bars: languages of records with a known language, per search, all questions together."
lang_known$lang2 <- ifelse(lang_known$language %in% sami_codes, "smi", lang_known$language)
t <- table(factor(lang_known$condition, conds), lang_known$lang2)
top <- names(sort(colSums(t), decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(5, ncol(t))]
tt <- cbind(t[, top, drop = FALSE], other = rowSums(t[, setdiff(colnames(t), top), drop = FALSE]))
share <- prop.table(tt, 1)
lang_names <- c(fin = "Finnish", swe = "Swedish", eng = "English", smi = "Sámi", sme = "Northern Sámi",
                nor = "Norwegian", deu = "German", other = "Other")
cols <- c("#C9A227", "#4F8FBF", "#B5523B", "#5B8C5A", "#8A6FA8", "#9AA5AB")[seq_len(ncol(share))]
chart_par(mar = c(4, 9, 1, 9), xpd = TRUE)
graphics::barplot(t(share[rev(conds), , drop = FALSE]), horiz = TRUE, col = cols, border = "white",
                  names.arg = cond_short[rev(conds)], xlab = "Share of records with a known language")
graphics::legend("right", inset = c(-0.28, 0), legend = ifelse(colnames(share) %in% names(lang_names), lang_names[colnames(share)], colnames(share)),
                 fill = cols, border = NA, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
n_known <- table(factor(lang_known$condition, conds)); n_all <- table(factor(rec_use$condition, conds))
smi_n <- if ("smi" %in% colnames(t)) t[, "smi"] else c(0, 0, 0)
```
<p class="how-to-read">How to read this: each bar is one search, all questions together. The
coloured parts show which languages its records are in, counting only records whose language
is known.</p>

```{r}
k <- data.frame(Search = cond_short,
                `Records` = as.integer(n_all), `Language known` = as.integer(n_known),
                Finnish = pct(share[, "fin"]), Swedish = pct(share[, "swe"]), English = pct(share[, "eng"]),
                check.names = FALSE)
if ("smi" %in% colnames(share)) k$`Sámi` <- pct(share[, "smi"])
tbl(k)
```

**What it means.** Our English key words mostly find English-language records and records
with no language at all (photographs and objects). The thesaurus terms in C bring
Finnish-language records forward (`r pct(share["A_direct", "fin"])` → `r pct(share["C_finto", "fin"])`)
and Swedish-language records (`r pct(share["A_direct", "swe"])` → `r pct(share["C_finto", "swe"])`).
`r if ("smi" %in% colnames(share)) paste0("Sámi-language records go the other way (", pct(share["A_direct", "smi"]), " → ", pct(share["C_finto", "smi"]), ", or ", smi_n[1], " records → ", smi_n[3], "): the study added Finnish, Swedish and English terms only, so the national languages took space in the top 60 that Sámi-language records had held. This is a clear example of how a standard vocabulary can shift *whose* material is visible.") else ""`
`r if (have_sami) { s <- sami_summary; paste0("The [Sámi test](extra-tests.qmd) checks this directly: when search C also used the thesaurus's Northern Sámi names, it kept **", s$focus_records_alt, "** Sámi-language records instead of ", s$focus_records_base, ".") } else ""`

**Be careful.** Only **`r pct(lang_known_share)`** of all kept records have a language at
all; most are images and objects. Read these shares as "among records with a language".

## 6. The types of material shift

```{r}
mt <- table(factor(rec_use$condition, conds), rec_use$material_type)
topm <- names(sort(colSums(mt), decreasing = TRUE))[1:min(6, ncol(mt))]
ms <- prop.table(mt, 1)[, topm, drop = FALSE]
md <- data.frame(Search = cond_short, apply(ms, 2, pct), check.names = FALSE)
tbl(md)
mat <- vis[vis$dimension == "material" & vis$from == "A_direct" & vis$question_id %in% usable_q, ]
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart: material types, share of records in searches A, B and C, all questions together."
draw_group_bars(pooled_counts("material"), pooled_n(), top = 8)
```

**What it means.** Images make up most records in every search, but their share falls in C,
while texts, journal articles and works of art come in. The median difference score for
material types between A and C is `r num(median(mat$jsd[mat$to == "C_finto"], na.rm = TRUE), 2)`.
`r noise_sentence(mat, "material types")`

## 7. The subject words change a lot

**What we measured.** The subject words that catalogues attached to the records, and how the
mix of subject words differs between searches.

```{r}
sub <- vis[vis$dimension == "subject" & vis$from == "A_direct" & vis$question_id %in% usable_q, ]
picks <- intersect(c("emigrant-letters", "womens-suffrage", "childrens-book-illustration"), usable_q)
ex <- do.call(rbind, lapply(picks, function(q) {
  th <- themes[themes$question_id == q, ]
  th$term <- sub("[.]+$", "", th$term)
  a <- head(unique(th$term[th$condition == "A_direct"]), 5)
  c <- unique(th$term[th$condition == "C_finto" & !th$in_A_top])
  data.frame(Question = qname(q), `Top subject words in A` = paste(a, collapse = ", "),
             `New top words in C` = paste(head(c, 5), collapse = ", "), check.names = FALSE)
}))
tbl(ex)
```

**What it means.** The subject words change more than anything else: the median difference
score between A and C is **`r num(median(sub$jsd[sub$to == "C_finto"], na.rm = TRUE), 2)`**.
`r noise_sentence(sub, "subject words")`
Partly this is simply language (*siirtolaiset* is Finnish for *emigrants*). Partly the
records really are about different things, so a researcher would build a different story from
them.

**Be careful.** The same idea written in two languages counts as two different subject
words here, which makes this difference look larger than it is.

## 8. Time coverage changes in some questions

```{r}
tm <- temporal[temporal$question_id %in% usable_q & temporal$records > 0, ]
tw <- reshape(tm[, c("question_id", "condition", "median")], idvar = "question_id", timevar = "condition", direction = "wide")
tw <- tw[match(usable_q, tw$question_id), ]
tw$shift <- tw$median.C_finto - tw$median.A_direct
out <- data.frame(Question = qname(tw$question_id), `Middle year A` = yr(tw$median.A_direct),
                  `Middle year B` = yr(tw$median.B_annif), `Middle year C` = yr(tw$median.C_finto),
                  `Change A to C (years)` = ifelse(is.na(tw$shift), "-", sprintf("%+d", round(tw$shift))), check.names = FALSE)
tbl(out)
big <- tw[!is.na(tw$shift) & abs(tw$shift) >= 5, ]
```

**What it means.** For most questions the period stays the same (the year range is fixed in
the search). In `r nrow(big)` questions the middle year moves by five years or more,
`r if (nrow(big)) paste0("for example ", paste0(qname(big$question_id), " (", sprintf("%+d", round(big$shift)), " years)", collapse = ", ")) else ""`.
The thesaurus terms can reach older or newer material than our own words do.

## All the main numbers in one table

```{r}
s <- metrics[metrics$question_id %in% usable_q, ]
agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(conds, function(c) {
  x <- s[s$condition == c, ]
  data.frame(Search = cond_short[c],
             `Search words (average)` = num(mean(x$query_terms), 1),
             `Matching records (middle value)` = num(median(x$index_matches)),
             `Records kept (average)` = num(mean(x$records), 1),
             `Institutions (average)` = num(mean(x$institutions), 1),
             `Found only through new words` = pct(mean(x$expansion_dependent_share, na.rm = TRUE)),
             `Match hidden` = pct(mean(x$unobserved_match_share, na.rm = TRUE)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
tbl(agg)
```

*Found only through new words* is the share of records that only match through a word added by
Annif or the thesaurus. *Match hidden* is the share where none of the search words can be seen
in the part of the record Finna shows us (see [How it works](how-it-works.qmd#why-was-each-record-found)).

The ready-made figures for the paper are in `results/final/paper/`; [Paper figures](paper-figures.qmd)
shows and explains them.
